platformBaselineOwner: security-and-lifecycle.md (AR-06, DR-126); this matrix asserts platform-invariant design only and no QUALIFIED cell

capabilityIdLaw.standing: Normative and CLOSED. THE vocabulary authority for analysis-spec requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId, for product-configuration analysis.capabilities, and for the authenticated release declaration registry. Published here because this document is already the closed capability x languageMode matrix; nothing new is invented, what was missing was the statement that this is the authority.
capabilityIdLaw.canonicalSpelling: Exactly the `id` strings above, byte for byte. They match the product-configuration analysis.capabilities item pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9._:-]*$, which contains no `@` - so the relation@rung spelling was never admissible at the configuration layer and must not be admissible at the analysis-spec layer either. Case, separators and aliases are not caller choices: an unknown or alias id refuses (native.requested-capability-unregistered).
capabilityIdLaw.whyThisWasNeeded: analysis-spec requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId is `$ref: #/$defs/Text` and enters PlanId through analysisSpecDigest, and no document named the vocabulary it is drawn from. Three spellings were in live use in one release: the reference default-selection corpus emitted relation@rung (`clones@normalized-body-hash`), the foundation reference fixture emitted `references`, and this matrix publishes `inventory`/`syntax`/`clones-fact`/`clones-near`/`clones-cross-tsjs`/`unresolved-edge`. Two conforming hosts requesting the same analysis of the same unit therefore mint different analysisSpecDigests, different PlanIds and different RunIds, which defeats independent replay across machines. The languageMode sibling was already closed against a registered map at Run closure; the capability was not, and that asymmetry is what this closes.
capabilityIdLaw.relationToRelationAtRung: A capability id and a relation@rung are DIFFERENT CONCEPTS and are not equated. A capability is a REQUESTABLE UNIT OF WORK and may cover several relations (`inventory` covers file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared and vcs-change@vcs-reported; `syntax` covers the three syntactic rungs) or none at all (`clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs` are candidate-only and bear no fact relation). A relation@rung is a FACT/COVERAGE COORDINATE: it is what CoverageKeyV2, the section 1.3 table, the grammar capability registry and the relation ladders speak. The bridge in BOTH directions is this document's own `capabilities[].relations`, so an implementer never has to guess one from the other. Substituting either spelling for the other is refused rather than silently accepted.
capabilityIdLaw.modeApplicability: A request names a capability AND a languageMode. The (capability, mode) cell must exist in `cells` - the table is the complete product of `capabilities` x `languageModes`, so it always does for registered members - and its `state` must not be NOT-SELECTED, which means `outside D-371; no promise` and is therefore an unsatisfiable request rather than a disclosable one (native.requested-capability-mode-not-selected). An UNSUPPORTED-TYPED cell IS requestable and is the case the unavailable-request disclosure exists for: it is answered with `unknown`, the cell's own named deficiency and its cause, never refused outright. The three NOT-SELECTED cells today are clones-cross-tsjs under rust-cargo, rust-cargo-prepared and syntax-only.

releaseDeclarationRegistry.standing: The `authenticated release declaration registry` named by native-evidence section 1.4 and admission-and-qualification section 1.1. Its CONTENT is release-specific and remains an authenticated INPUT - which rows a given release ships is not a contract constant - but its SCHEMA, its membership authority, its canonical spelling and its binding to the Plan are normative and are stated here.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.membershipAuthority: capabilityId MUST be a member of this document's capabilities[].id, and every entry of languageModes MUST be a member of this document's languageModes with a cell that is not NOT-SELECTED. A row spelled preview-* is refused, as it already was. A row may never name a member the matrix does not register.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.bindingToPlan: default_capability_selection emits one analysis-spec row per (unit, capability REQUIRED BY THE MATRIX for that unit's languageMode) - see requiredDefault - with required=true, provenance=DEFAULTED, in canonical-set order, and a duplicate refuses rather than silently deduping. The emitted capabilityId is the matrix id, so the DEFAULT and EXPLICIT paths agree on one vocabulary by construction. An earlier revision of THIS sentence said one row per (registry row, unit), which was the release-driven recipe requiredDefault replaces; two normative recipes cannot both stand, and this is the one.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.notASubstituteForAdmission: The default helper is one producer of an analysis-spec, not the authority. The same vocabulary is closed again where it matters - at Plan/Run closure over the RETAINED analysis-spec - so an explicitly configured or hand-built spec is judged by the same rule as a defaulted one.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.itIsAvailabilityNotScope: NORMATIVE, and the correction of an earlier sentence that read `the registry may declare a SUBSET of the matrix - a release need not ship everything`. That sentence was written about MEMBERSHIP and read as permission about SCOPE. The registry states which capabilities THIS BUILD SHIPS. It never states which capabilities the product SELECTS: that is fixed by this matrix, and admission section 1.1 and native section 1.4 both require the `default` profile to be the complete intended product. Driving the default FROM the registry let a staged build shipping three rows silently request three capabilities and still look conformant, which is the D-371 selected product quietly shrinking with nothing disclosed anywhere.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.requiredDefault: For each discovered unit the `default` profile MUST request EVERY capability whose (capability, unit languageMode) cell is not NOT-SELECTED - that is the published definition of the selected product, since NOT-SELECTED means `outside D-371; no promise`. UNSUPPORTED-TYPED cells are INCLUDED deliberately: the matrix says such a cell `refuses with the named deficiency; never silently narrows`, and the way it never silently narrows is that the default asks and the Run answers with the disclosed unavailable pair. Omitting it would leave a consumer with no record that the capability exists and was not served.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.absenceIsDisclosedNotDropped: A capability the selected product requires and this release does not declare available is still REQUESTED, and the selection boundary records the absence in default_capability_selection's `undeclaredCapabilities`. That record is an AVAILABILITY ACCOUNT, not a CoverageResultV3 and not a final (deficiency, nativeCause) pair - see absenceProjectionAndPrecedence. No new vocabulary, no new public code, and no preview or default exception.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.installedAvailabilityVersusQualification: Declaring availability is NOT qualification and cannot promote a cell. platformQualified stays false, no cell is QUALIFIED here, and SUPPORTED-DESIGN remains `contracted behavior, corpus named, qualification pending` whatever a release declares. A staged or development build that ships fewer providers is an availability fact disclosed per request; it is not a narrowed product, not a completed release qualification, and not a licence to restate the matrix.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.explicitOverride: Explicit user configuration - product-configuration analysis.capabilities, same vocabulary - overrides the REQUEST, not this obligation. An override is a recorded choice carrying its own provenance (the default's is DEFAULTED); it is a user narrowing their own analysis, which is visible, and never a host silently narrowing the product, which would not be.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.hostInputBoundary: Stated honestly: WHICH rows a release ships is an authenticated input this contract cannot measure, and nothing here qualifies a build, an installer or a provider. What is contract is the obligation the default must meet, the vocabulary and membership the declaration is held to, and the disclosure an absence owes.
releaseDeclarationRegistry.absenceProjectionAndPrecedence: What an absence PROJECTS to depends on the capability, and neither case may be assumed. (1) PRECEDENCE. A capability can be undeclared AND unservable by the admitted universe at the same time - references under syntax-only is both. The syntax capability prerequisite DERIVES language-tier-unsupported / capability-missing for such a scope and refuses anything else, and the section 10 precedence ranks language-tier-unsupported ahead of provider-unavailable, so the more specific one wins and the release-absence account never overrides it. The final Coverage pair remains the owning derivation's. Where no more specific deficiency applies, provider-unavailable with capability-missing is the applicable pair, routed by section 10 to the existing COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE. (2) CANDIDATE-ONLY CAPABILITIES. clones-near and clones-cross-tsjs have EMPTY `relations` here: they are candidate-only by section 6.1 authority, mint no fact and no relation@rung, and therefore have NO Coverage entry that could carry a pair. Requiring an owed Coverage for them would mean fabricating a relation. Their absence account is the selection record itself, projection `selection-account-only`; fact-producing capabilities carry projection `coverage-entry` and name the exact relation@rung coordinates they project onto. An availability account may be shared by all capabilities; it is not automatically a CoverageResultV3 for any of them.

capabilityIdLaw.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model admit_requested_capabilities (the analysis-spec boundary) and admit_release_capability_registry (the authenticated input boundary), and again at identity-model.v3.open_run_closure over the retained analysis-spec (native owner admission), beside the languageMode join that was already there. identity-model.v3.close_run is complete evaluator3 replay, not a second native vocabulary helper.
capabilityIdLaw.unchanged: No capability is added, removed or renamed; no cell state changes; the six advertised language modes, the native contexts and the full default-selected product all stay exactly as representable as before. This publishes the authority for a field that had none.

limitations.L-JS1: synthesized options: paths/baseUrl/rootDirs/custom types unknown; such specifiers are unresolved-module-specifier edges
limitations.L-JS2: dynamic JavaScript forms (computed member access, non-literal require/import(), indirect eval, reflective access, any-typed calls) are unresolved edges; universal negatives are then resolution-incomplete
limitations.L-JS3: types@checked facts on JavaScript subjects without annotation or JSDoc carry derivationKind=compiler-inferred; exact under the admitted universe, no probabilistic confidence; rule packs may require derivationPolicy=declared-only
limitations.L-RS1: every activated non-path Cargo.lock package must be in the sealed dependency source set; otherwise dependent crates' semantic rungs are input-closure-incomplete
limitations.L-RS2: dyn Trait and generic-bound calls resolve to the trait method declaration and are recorded as dynamic-dispatch unresolved edges
limitations.L-RS3: non-prepared mode: external proc-macro invocations and build-script outputs are unavailable; generated-dependent types are input-closure-incomplete (generated-output-unavailable)
limitations.L-RS4: prepared mode consumes only inert expansion/directive rows; a site without a matching row is macro-expansion-unavailable
limitations.L-FW1: reachability universal negatives need an origin set; unrecognized frameworks without explicit origins yield resolution-incomplete (entry-point-unrecognized)
limitations.L-CL1: cross-tsjs candidates use tsjs-erasure-v1 syntax projection; bodies with runtime-significant TypeScript tokens are excluded; never a fact, never a deletion prerequisite
limitations.inventory: Inventory relations are produced by the shared discovery rule and the VCS observation; no compiler, provider or grammar is executed for them. Naming the producing component here qualifies no platform and measures nothing.
limitations.syntaxOnlyGrammarClass: The host bundles grammars for seven languages: rust, typescript, javascript (syntaxClass code) and json, toml, markdown, yaml (syntaxClass data-document). Code grammars have the section 6.3 body spans and the published L2/L3 normalisation tables, so they bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations. Data/document grammars are bundled and accounted - their files are grammar-only members bearing inventory evidence, never unsupported-file - but this kit publishes no tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law for them, so they mint no body identity and produce no code-construct fact. The syntax and clones cells above are qualified accordingly; nothing that was previously representable has been narrowed, and data-format syntax facts remain a bounded future capability that would need a published tokenisation law first.

jsOptionSemantics.allowJs: admits .js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx roots into the TypeScript program (source: typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs, read 2026-09-06); it is a program-membership option
jsOptionSemantics.checkJs: enables diagnostics for JavaScript files (source: typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/checkJs, read 2026-09-06); it changes reported errors, not what is resolved; it is a universe key, not a capability gate
jsOptionSemantics.resolutionCompleteness: claimed only by CoverageV3.resolutionCompleteness after resolution was attempted over an exhaustive examined partition with a complete stage; neither allowJs nor checkJs implies it

cells.note: bundled grammars only; a language with no bundled grammar is language-tier-unsupported
no resolution is attempted, so no unresolved edges are observed
